Encore 0.6.0 (draft): Encore finds songs on its own now. No more Python,
Deno or yt-dlp to download, and nothing to set up.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.6.0_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.6.0_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.6.0_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.6.0_amd64.AppImage` |

Encore 0.5 updates itself to this version. Updating keeps your session,
settings and downloads.

## What's new

- **Nothing to set up.** Encore used to download yt-dlp and the Python and
  Deno it runs on before it could play anything. It now finds a song's audio
  itself, with an extractor that follows yt-dlp's and yt-dlp's own
  challenge solver built into the app. The setup screen is gone.
- **120 to 160 MB back.** The first launch of 0.6.0 removes the player
  components 0.5 downloaded. Nothing else in Encore's folders is touched.
- **Clearer reasons.** When a song can't play, Encore says why: a bot check,
  a song that isn't available in your country, an age restriction, a live
  stream. When YouTube changes something only a newer Encore can follow,
  the message and **Settings → Playback** say so.
- **Settings → Playback → Player engine** shows what Encore plays with, and
  can reset its player cache.
- **Downloads** take their loudness from the same request that finds the
  song, so a new download needs one request less.

## Fixed

- Signed out, Encore sent no visitor id to YouTube Music, because YouTube's
  visitor ids grew longer than Encore accepted.
- Cookies YouTube sets with its usual expiry date format were dropped as if
  they had expired.
